intro: Sonnet 5.5 lands a day after Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Sol/Luna reset model pricing; Bitcoin drifts near $83,000 on Iran-driven macro pressure. Dev Tools is a security-heavy day.

items.headline: Anthropic ships Claude Sonnet 5.5, with Terminal-Bench 4.0 at 70.6%
items.summary: Sonnet 5.5 keeps Sonnet 5 pricing ($2/$10 per million tokens) while generating output more than 30% faster and, per Anthropic, costing up to 30% less per task. Claude Code users running Sonnet with thinking disabled must move to the new between_tools setting before upgrading.
items.why: Near-Opus agentic-coding scores at Sonnet prices change the default model calculus for coding agents.

items.headline: Cursor launches Rollouts and Security Review bots for Teams and Enterprise
items.summary: Rollouts monitors changes as they deploy across environments, while Security Review flags exploitable vulnerabilities such as injection issues in pull requests and proposes fixes.
items.why: Agent vendors are moving from writing code to policing deployment and security.

items.headline: Opus 5.5 brings Fable 5.1-level performance at $4/$20 per million tokens
items.summary: Anthropic reports 66.4% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and 81.8% on OSWorld 2.1, with output over 30% faster than Opus 5 and a 1M-token context window.
items.why: Cheaper top-tier agentic coding, released Sept 22 and now the default Opus in Claude Code.

items.headline: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Sol and Luna at roughly half the prior price
items.summary: Sol is priced at $2/$10 and Luna at $0.10/$0.50 per million tokens, bringing Astra-generation capability and alignment gains to faster, cheaper models in the API, Codex and ChatGPT.
items.why: Sets a new price floor for capable models, following Anthropic's Opus 5.5 release about 90 minutes earlier.

items.headline: Anthropic Sonnet 5.5 benchmarks: near-Opus knowledge-work scores
items.summary: Anthropic says Sonnet 5.5 scores nearly level with Opus 5.5 on GDPval-AA and reaches 55.5% on CursorBench, within about two points of Opus 5.5.
items.why: Mid-tier models are closing the gap with flagships, which affects cost/quality tradeoffs.

items.headline: GitHub Actions workflow execution protections reach general availability
items.summary: Owners can allowlist who may trigger workflows and which events can start them, scoped to specific workflow files, with audit insights and a REST API. Public repositories now default to having pull_request_target disabled.
items.why: A direct hardening step against CI supply-chain attacks.

items.headline: GitHub adds proof of presence for high-impact actions
items.summary: Enterprise members must re-authenticate or pass a multi-factor challenge before sensitive actions. It is currently available for managed-user enterprises using Microsoft Entra ID.
items.why: Limits the blast radius of stolen credentials in enterprise orgs.

items.headline: Bitcoin slips to about $83,000 as Trump rejects Iran's 7-day plan
items.summary: BTC traded near $82,958 on Monday, a strong dollar, higher yields and Brent crude above $100 weighing on crypto. It is up 4.1% on the week but down 23% year over year.
items.why: Geopolitics and oil-driven rate expectations are the main near-term price drivers.

items.headline: US spot Bitcoin ETFs turn net positive for 2026
items.summary: Cumulative inflows recovered from a $5.8 billion deficit in July to about $800 million net for the year, still far below the $35.2 billion of 2024 and $21.4 billion of 2025.
items.why: Institutional demand has returned, though at a much smaller scale than prior years.
